senses.gloss: Happening through bad luck, or because of some unfortunate event.
Any member of the family Canidae, including canines (dogs, wolves, coyotes and jackals) and vulpines (foxes).
plural of person: a body of persons considered generally or collectively; a group of two or more persons.
A measure of the extent of a surface; it is measured in square units.
land area free of woodland, cities, and towns; open country
A bounded or specific extent, physical or otherwise.
A particular area of study.
(sports) The position of a team in a league or of a player in a list.
Something characterized by a square, or nearly square, form.
The physical means or contrivances to make something (especially a public service) possible; the required equipment, infrastructure, location etc. [from 19th c.]

(historical) A member of a group of Sarmatian tribes, nomadic pastoralists of the 1st millennium AD who spoke an Eastern Iranian language derived from Scytho-Sarmatian and which in turn evolved into modern Ossetian.
Money which is sent to someone, typically to someone in another country.
To quarantine or isolate oneself from others, especially in order to avoid spreading a communicable disease.
Unalterable, capable of being read but not written.
Relating to the internal mechanics of a market rather than more basic factors.
The practical aspects of a given art, occupation etc.; formal requirements.
Still to be paid; owed as a debt.
A sovereign state with dominant status on the globe and a very advanced military, especially the United States or formerly the Soviet Union.
A planet which exists outside Earth's solar system.
(countable) an instance of shooting with a gun or other weapon
The empty shell of a marine mollusk.
A moving disturbance in the level of a body of liquid; an undulation.
A sudden increase.
To become a member of.
An item of information put into a temporary or permanent physical medium.
The act of registering for something; registration.
The act of signing up or registering for something.
(computing) The process or an instance of logging in.
A qualification or exemption.
partly frozen, crystalline state of water that falls from the atmosphere as precipitation in flakes; falling of such flakes; accumulation of them as a white layer
(uncountable) Interference on a broadcast signal caused by atmospheric disturbances; heard as crackles on radio, or seen as random specks on television.
Money, riches, or wealth, especially when seen as having a corrupting effect or causing greed, or obtained in an underhanded manner.
A large, black grouse of the genus Tetrao in the bird family Phasianidae, especially the western capercaillie, Tetrao urogallus.
ache or bodily suffering
Continued dull pain, as distinguished from sudden twinges, or spasmodic pain.
A competition to determine a champion, especially the final of a series of competitions.
The technical skills and fluent style of a virtuoso.
A specific version, edition, translation, or copy of one of the above-mentioned book.
Strongly or sublimely good, beautiful, or pleasurable.
Any small parrot from one of the nine species within the genus Agapornis. Sometimes they are kept as cage birds and are noted for their affection towards each other.
The metal bar forming part of the track for a railroad.
The downwards force an object experiences due to gravity.
physics: quantity of matter which a body contains
Influence, weight, or authority that inclines to one side
(informal) Influence or effectiveness, especially political.
(archaic) Hence, any weight.
(dated, except, UK, dialectal, and, US) The force exerted by an object due to gravitation; weight.
The quality or state of being slow.
A post bearing a sign that gives information on directions.
Capable of working together without conflict.
Capable of being adapted or of adapting; susceptible of or undergoing accordant change.
Of, relating to, or enforced by a contract.
Affording, or disposed to afford, accommodation; obliging; helpful.
Having components pleasingly or appropriately combined.
Capable of being adapted.
(symbol: ⊇) With respect to another set, a set such that each of the elements of the other set is also an element of the set.
A critically endangered salamander found in the elevated lakes of Mexico, Ambystoma mexicanum.
A flying insect of the order Lepidoptera, distinguished from moths by their diurnal activity and generally brighter colouring.
A folding pocket knife with two handles counter-rotating around the tang such that, when closed, the blade is concealed within grooves in the handles.
Liked, cherished.
Facial hair reaching from the top of the head down the side of the face to the side of the chin.
Occurring for no particular reason; haphazard, unpredictable.
Coming without regularity; occasional or incidental.
In a random manner.
Made up of various disparate elements mixed together; of disorderly composition.
Random; chaotic; incomplete; not thorough, constant, or consistent.
In a haphazard manner; in a random, chaotic, and incomplete manner.
Pertaining to the adrenal glands (suprarenal glands), their secretions, or the function derived therefrom.
Place or position.
The residential area near one's home.
administrative subdivision of cities
Any subdivision of a conurbation, not necessarily on the periphery.
An evergreen shrub or small tree, Pistacia lentiscus (mastic tree), native to the Mediterranean.
The state of being loyal; fidelity.
Faithfulness to God and one's religion.
The state or act of keeping faith; constancy of support.
The action of the verb to sew.
An arrangement of stitches in sewing, or method of stitching in some particular way or style.
A place where things join, a junction.
(anatomy) A type of fibrous joint bound together by Sharpey's fibres which only occurs in the skull.
The art or process of working with a needle especially in embroidery or needlepoint.
fine work done by stitching
Act or instance of running, of moving rapidly using the feet.
The action of the verb to run.
The sport of competing in races.
The act or action of the verb to sprint (to run, cycle, etc. at top speed for a short period).
(zoology) Having legs fitted for running.
A Muslim who has memorized the whole Qur'an.
A chronological collection of pictures or short videos published by a user on an application or website that is typically only available for a short period.
Any of several yellow-flowered cruciferous weeds of grain fields, especially wild mustard (Rhamphospermum arvense, syn. Sinapis arvensis).
A particular aspect, feature or detail of something.

The measure of such a figure. In the case of a plane angle, this is the ratio (or proportional to the ratio) of the arc length to the radius of a section of a circle cut by the two rays, centered at their common point. In the case of a solid angle, this is the ratio of the surface area to the square of the radius of the section of a sphere.
A small corner formed by two walls; an alcove.
(vulgar, US) An imaginary place in the middle of nowhere.
The Austroasiatic language spoken predominantly in Vietnam.
someone of mixed kind
Of mixed heritage
person of mixed ancestry
To yield or make concession.
(chiefly, British, and, Australian, legal) A person who operates a motor vehicle when legally intoxicated.
person devoted to studying philosophy
Resembling milk in color, consistency, smell, etc.; consisting of milk.
(science) Possessing or pertaining to energy. [from 19th c.]
Lively and vigorous.
Full of pep; energetic, cheerful, and vigorous; bouncy
Not given enough recognition for its quality.
Having or showing ambition; wanting a lot of power, honor, respect, superiority, or other distinction.
Idealistic, implying over-optimism.
The bubonic plague, the pestilent disease caused by the virulent bacterium Yersinia pestis.
(by extension) An obnoxious person or troublemaker.

(countable, veterinary disease, chiefly, historical) Any of several highly infectious diseases of cattle or other livestock, such as anthrax, babesiosis, or rinderpest; or a particular epizootic thereof; also, an infectious disease affecting other animals, such as poultry.
Not speaking; indisposed to talk; speechless; mute; taciturn; not loquacious; not talkative.
Not having the power of speech; dumb.
A mollusc from genus Octopus.
(medicine) An abnormal growth protruding from a mucous membrane.

A solemn, authentic instrument in writing, by which a person declares his or her will as to disposal of his or her inheritance (estate and effects) after his or her death, benefiting specified heir(s).
The transfer of property upon the owner's death according to the will of the deceased.

A sterol lipid synthesized by the liver and transported in the bloodstream to the membranes of all animal cells; it plays a central role in many biochemical processes and, as a lipoprotein that coats the walls of blood vessels, is associated with cardiovascular disease.
To make (a person) angry, distressed, or unhappy.
To cause sorrow or distress to.
To make sad or unhappy.
Grass of other species of genus Phleum.
A penis.
Of, from, or pertaining to Morocco or the Moroccan people.
(British spelling) Of or pertaining to behaviour.
Of or pertaining to agriculture.
Having a curve or curves; curving.
A person who bakes and sells bread, cakes and similar items.
To take a subject at higher level without having previously studied it.
A compact folding knife.
A small pocketknife; (loosely) any pocketknife.
A knife small enough for carrying safely and handily in a pocket; usually a folding knife (with blades or tools that the user can fold or retract into the handle).
to mend or repair
To restore to good working order, fix, or improve damaged condition; to mend; to remedy.
to bring back to a previous condition or state
To physically repair (something that is broken, defaced, decayed, torn, or otherwise damaged).
To fiddle with something in an attempt to fix, mend or improve it, especially in an experimental or unskilled manner.
To renew; to revamp something to make it look new again.
The territory ruled by a tsar.
To remove a cover from.
The socialist and communist philosophy and political program founded by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.
Avoidance of saying or reluctance to say too much; discretion, tight-lippedness; (countable) an instance of acting in this manner.
The claim or pretense of having beliefs, standards, qualities, behaviours, virtues, motivations, etc. which one does not really have.
Intentional deceptiveness; double-dealing.
A cosmetic used to darken and thicken the eyelashes.
The part of milk that coagulates when it sours or is treated with enzymes; used to make cottage cheese, dahi, etc.
A temporary stop or rest; an intermission of action; interruption; suspension; cessation.
temporary stoppage of an activity — see also break, pause
A break for a worker or workers that splits a period of work.
A prokaryotic organism; a member of the domain Archaea [from 20th c.]
Inflammation of the tonsils.
A forefather, any of a person's direct ancestors.
A sound or action like liquid hitting a hard surface, or an object falling into a body of water.
The eighth month of the Roman, Julian, and Gregorian calendars, following July and preceding September.

A facility that melts metals in special furnaces and pours the molten metal into molds to make products. Foundries are usually specified according to the type of metal dealt with: iron foundry, brass foundry, etc.
The quality of being impulsive, impulsiveness; inclination to act on impulse rather than thought.
The faculty of thinking, judging, abstract reasoning, and conceptual understanding; the cognitive faculty.
(music) A ceremonious passage such as a fanfare.
The land of city states of the Phoenicians which around 1000 BC was situated on the coast of present day Syria and Lebanon, and included the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
Very remarkable; highly extraordinary; amazing.
Observant of tradition; attached to old customs; old-fashioned.
A satirical imitation of a work of art or a genre.
A city in Iran, the seat of Hamadan County's Central District and the capital of Hamadan Province.
The islands off the west coast of Scotland, divided into the Inner Hebrides and the Outer Hebrides.
Kinship; being related by blood or marriage.
A silvery metallic chemical element with an atomic number of 39, mainly found in combination with lanthanide elements in rare earth minerals.
Moving or progressing faster than is usual.
The study of landforms, their classification, origin, development, and history.
An herbaceous plant, species Tussilago farfara, that grows in Europe and the Middle East; yellow coltsfoot.
The act by which something is cured.
Disparaging, belittling or derogatory.
An appendage used for sensing on the head of an insect, crab, or other animal.
An antenna or appendage used for feeling, especially on an insect.

(immunology, cytology) A white blood cell that phagocytizes necrotic cell debris and foreign material, including viruses, bacteria, and tattoo ink. It presents foreign antigens on MHC II to lymphocytes. Part of the innate immune system.
A waiter who has a supervisory position over the other wait staff; chief waiter.
A sedative of the benzodiazepine class, used (as the hydrochloride) chiefly as a premedication for anesthesia; 8-chloro-6-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-4H-imidazo[1,5-a][1,4]benzodiazepine, C₁₈H₁₃ClFN₃.
A lightweight, two-wheeled vehicle equipped with a small motor and pedals, designed to go no faster than some specified speed limit.
A person who is zealously enthusiastic for some cause.
a dreamlike or pensive composition
An ideology which claims that the military is the foundation of a society's security, and thereby its most important aspect.
A geographical region in southern South America, including the southern parts of Chile and Argentina.
Trouble; troublesome business; fuss, commotion.
A confused sound of a crowd of people shouting or speaking simultaneously; an uproar.
(countable) A series of boat races, or sometimes a single race.

A metal urn with a spigot, for boiling water for making tea. Traditionally, the water is heated by hot coals or charcoal in a chimney-like tube which runs through the center of the urn. Today, it is more likely that the water is heated by an electric coil.

An illustrated outline filled in with a solid color(s), usually only black, and intended to represent the shape of an object without revealing any other visual details; a similar appearance produced when the object being viewed is situated in relative darkness with brighter lighting behind it; a profile portrait in black, such as a shadow appears to be.

Any of three species of large seabird in the genus Morus, of the family Sulidae. They have black and white bodies and long pointed wings, and hunt for fish by plunge diving and pursuing their prey underwater.
A plant of the genus Iris, common in the northern hemisphere, and generally having attractive blooms (See Iris (plant) on Wikipedia.Wikipedia ).
A group of many islands.

A part of speech that indicates, specifies and limits a noun (a, an, or the in English). In some languages the article may appear as an ending (e.g. definite article in Swedish) or there may be none (e.g. Russian, Pashto).
In a typographical manner.
To (cause something to) tremble or quiver.
An entry posted on the microblogging service Twitter.
A vibraphone.
A percussion instrument with a double row of tuned metal bars, each above a tubular resonator containing a motor-driven rotating vane, giving a vibrato effect.
Any of the medium-sized to large feliform carnivores of the family Hyaenidae, native to Africa and Asia and noted for the sound similar to laughter which they can make if excited.
Rheum; sleepy dust.
Any of various small freshwater ducks of the genus Anas that are brightly coloured and have short necks.
Smooth, even, aligned; not sticking out.
showing wickedness typical of a devil
